Expectation1: Ensuring financial stability for the family
Situation1: The family requires money for daily living expenses, and the step-parent needs to provide it
Expectation2: Raise public awareness about social inequities and marginalized groups
Situation2: They respond to an urgent incident of discrimination that requires immediate public attention and awareness.
Story: I sat at the kitchen table, bills spread out before me, the numbers blurring together. As a step-parent, I knew my family depended on me to keep the lights on, to make sure there was food in the fridge. My partner’s hours had been cut, and the kids needed new shoes for school. Every dollar mattered. Just as I was calculating how to stretch our budget, my phone buzzed. A message from the advocacy group: a local incident of discrimination had just occurred, and they needed me to help organize a rally and speak to the press—tonight. My heart pounded. I’d promised to pick up an extra shift at work, the only way to cover this month’s rent. But the cause was urgent, and my voice could make a difference. I felt torn, the weight of my family’s needs pressing against the call to stand up for justice. Both roles demanded all of me, right now, and I didn’t know how to choose.
